propositions: The byte-equivalence oracle invokes a redundant copied `_legacy_convert` subprocess for all 884 prepared corpus units, sharing mutable `_PANDOC_TO` constant with production and failing to independently detect format mutations.

Immutable golden-output fixture with platform-keyed Pandoc version and binary SHA-256 metadata replaces the copied legacy subprocess while preserving all 884 real production `_convert` Pandoc calls per CI run.
Schema v2 maps both darwin-arm64 and linux-x86_64 Pandoc binary fingerprints; platform-stable key selects exact supported hash and fails closed on version drift, platform mismatch, or incomplete map.
Measured local savings: 32.3766 seconds and 884 eliminated subprocesses; production conversion latency and hardening scope unchanged.
All 884 prepared corpus units pass through production `_convert` with real Pandoc; mutation to plain format makes independent byte-equivalence oracle RED.
Deterministic regeneration retains both platform fingerprints; CI gates (Ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS arm64) pass with exact version and binary validation.
